notes: Second full sweep: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) at db91c23 with no uncommitted changes (skill_hash a6a9c1d6...); every run has rc 0 and a model_id matching its tier.

Validate input with changesets changed since 93873be and is graded against the current text of idiomatic-elixir/references/ecto-phoenix.md, ## Validate input with changesets. Three sentences now decide: "A `%User{}` built from the params and passed to `Repo.insert/1` is the pattern to replace: Ecto inserts the struct as given, so nothing is validated and a constraint violation raises.", "`Repo.update/2` does not accept a struct at all; it raises `ArgumentError`, and only a changeset can carry the changes." and "Declare database constraints in the changeset (`unique_constraint/3`, and `foreign_key_constraint/3` or `assoc_constraint/3` for a `belongs_to`) so a violation returns `{:error, changeset}` instead of raising."

Validate input with changesets, violating runs out of five per decisive sentence: bare struct passed to Repo.insert/1: 0 of 5 (every insert receives a changeset: the post through Post.changeset/2, the audit row through Log.changeset/2). Struct passed to Repo.update: 0 of 5 (every update of published_at receives a changeset from change/2 or a publish_changeset function). Missing user constraint: 1 of 5 (skill-haiku-1, lines 25-30; opus-1 line 26, haiku-2 line 27, sonnet-1 line 33 and sonnet-2 line 56 use assoc_constraint(:user)). The unchanged cast/3 paragraph is also 0 of 5: every run casts only [:title, :body] and sets user_id on the struct. In the previous sweep 1 of 5 skill runs (skill-haiku-2) left the constraint out, so the count is unchanged; all four runs that declared a constraint used assoc_constraint(:user), which the new text names.

Other rule text changed since 93873be (the one-step `with` sentences, two Naming bullets, one Enum table row) governs no rule in this case's list. Checked anyway: every `with` in the five runs has two `<-` steps, so the new one-step sentence finds nothing here.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because mix format, run without Ecto's and Phoenix's locals_without_parens, adds parentheses to field, belongs_to, add and similar calls. The grade file's format_ok comes from Code.format_string!/2 with the Ecto, Ecto SQL and Phoenix DSL calls (field, belongs_to, timestamps, from, add, alter, execute, remove and others) in locals_without_parens, as the previous sweep computed it; all five pass. Nothing compiles because Phoenix and Ecto are not installed.

Unchanged rules follow the previous sweep's standard. Keep migrations to schema changes is judged on the migration module; skill-haiku-2 is the first skill run across the previous sweep, the check batch and this sweep to backfill inside the migration, and its own comment says why: line 111: "# The backfill is in this migration because it was requested. It is raw SQL,". A missing @moduledoc on the MyApp.Blog context counts under the comments rule (haiku-1 line 38, haiku-2 line 37); a missing @moduledoc on the Post schema or missing @doc on schema functions does not (haiku-1 and haiku-2 Post modules), as the previous sweep did not count them.

skill-sonnet-2 calls change/2 in MyApp.Blog (line 118: |> change(published_at: DateTime.utc_now(:second))), but that module imports only Ecto.Query (line 65), so the file would not compile; the transcript shows import Ecto.Changeset only in Post from the first write. This is a correctness bug, not a rule violation: the value passed to Repo.update is meant to be a changeset.

Transcripts show every run reading SKILL.md and references/ecto-phoenix.md; skill-haiku-2 also read references/processes.md twice (and ecto-phoenix.md twice) without saying why, and wrote no process code.
